summary: requirements_analysis.md is a faithful, well-sourced extraction of design.md's OpenRouter-direct scope (§"Backend's own direct OpenRouter calls", lines 234-253; §"Backend's own OpenRouter calls (task enrichment, guardian, conductor)", lines 579-620; §Data Model, lines 254-311; Implementation Phase 5, lines 692-694). Every FR/NFR traces to a specific design.md line range. One minor unsourced addition found (see notes) but it is presented as an optional suggestion, not a mandatory requirement, so it does not constitute scope drift severe enough to fail the gate.

requirement_traceability.requirement: Enable OpenRouter usage/cost data (extra_body usage.include=true) on all orchestrator LLM calls
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: design.md lines 234-243: 'OpenRouter's non-standard usage.cost field ... is a one-line addition: model_kwargs={"extra_body": {..., "usage": {"include": True}}}'

requirement_traceability.requirement: Single choke-point helper (_invoke_and_record) wrapping all orchestrator model.ainvoke() call sites
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: design.md lines 589-600: 'add one private helper, e.g. _invoke_and_record(model, messages, component, task_id=None), and route all 9 call sites through it'
requirement_traceability.notes: Design.md estimates '~9' call sites (7 named + 'plus 2 more' unnamed); requirements_analysis.md reports 7 confirmed in the current repo via grep. This is a factual discrepancy between the design's estimate and the repo's actual state, not an omission or addition by the requirements doc — the requirement itself (route every call site through one helper) is unchanged and correctly traced.

requirement_traceability.requirement: Attribute cost entries to task/agent/workflow where known, else nullable overhead bucket
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: design.md lines 296-298 (task_id nullable, rolls up to overhead) and lines 602-614 (per-call-site task_id threading check)

requirement_traceability.requirement: Extract token counts and cost.total from OpenRouter response_metadata and write to CostEntry; live smoke-test gap explicitly called out
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: design.md lines 616-619 (wire _invoke_and_record once opt-in confirmed) and lines 245-252 (smoke test needed to confirm response_metadata survival) and lines 254-293 (CostEntry schema)

requirement_traceability.requirement: Raw usage payload retained on CostEntry.raw_usage for debugging
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: design.md lines 284-288: 'Raw source line/turn, kept for debugging discrepancies'

requirement_traceability.requirement: Cost-extraction failure must never break the underlying LLM call
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: Inferred from design.md's general framing of cost capture as additive instrumentation around existing call sites (lines 589-619); not a verbatim design.md statement
requirement_traceability.notes: The reliability requirement itself is a reasonable, narrow inference from design intent (cost capture must not be allowed to break primary functionality) and doesn't add new work. However, the specific implementation critique embedded in NFR-1 — 'narrow the except Exception: logger.debug(...) to distinguish no-cost-data from malformed-cost-data' — is not sourced from any design.md line; it is the analyst's own code-review observation of the existing implementation. It is phrased as an optional recommendation (repeated in §7 item 3 as 'Consider narrowing') rather than an acceptance criterion, so it is flagged here as an advisory addition for architecture_design to accept or drop, not a scope violation requiring correction back to product_requirements.

requirement_traceability.requirement: No double-instrumentation — one record_cost() call per _invoke_and_record invocation
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: Follows directly from the single-choke-point design (design.md lines 589-600) — a natural corollary, not separate new scope

requirement_traceability.requirement: Non-OpenRouter providers unaffected — cost_usd defaults to 0 and no CostEntry written when cost data absent
requirement_traceability.design_doc_reference: design.md lines 234-236 (OpenRouter-specific field) combined with the general CostEntry design (lines 266-293, cost_usd required, non-nullable) implies non-OpenRouter calls simply produce no entry

out_of_scope_items_correctly_excluded: Budget enforcement guards (cost_limit_usd checks, pause/resume) — design.md Implementation Phase 3, separately delivered per git log
Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex collector implementations — design.md Implementation Phases 4, 6, 8
Pi extension changes — design.md 'Pi Extension Collector' section, separate mechanism
UI budget configuration — design.md Implementation Phase 7
cost_derivation.py rollup logic and CostEntry/database.py schema — design.md Data Model (lines 254-311), correctly noted as 'not modified by this feature, only called'
requirements_analysis_items_not_traceabl: NFR-1's specific suggestion to narrow the except Exception handler to distinguish absent-vs-malformed cost data (see NFR-1 notes above) — advisory only, not blocking
notes: requirements_analysis.md §6 flags that .hephaestus/features/openrouter-direct/scope.md does not exist in this worktree, and that the analysis was scoped from the task assignment's inline in-scope/out-of-scope statement instead, cross-checked against design.md Implementation Phase 5. That in-scope/out-of-scope statement matches design.md's own phase boundaries (OpenRouter-direct is phase 5; budget enforcement is phase 3 and already shipped; Claude Code/OpenCode/Codex/UI are phases 4/6/7/8) — no drift introduced by using the task assignment as a scoping source in scope.md's absence.
